en.content: If 50% of a reaction occurs in 100 second and 75% of the reaction occurs in  200 secod, the order of this reaction is :

options.content: Zero

en.explanation:
Assume initial concentration of the reactant = 1 M

After 100 second, concentration becomes of the reactant

= 1 = 0.5 M

After 200 second, concentration of the reactant becomes

= 1 = 0.25 M.

So, in first 100 second reactant concentration becomes half of initial and in the second 100 second concentration becomes 0.5 M to 0.25 M, which is also half of 0.5 M.

So, after each 100 second period, concentration of reactant becomes half of initial concentration.

So, 100 second is the half life period and it is independent of concentration of reactant. This is characteristic of first order reaction.

Lactose contains <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.439ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="2.034ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -705 573 899" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FD" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FD"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-D-galactose and <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.439ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="2.034ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -705 573 899" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FD" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FD"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-D-glucose.

en.explanation:
(a) Both maltose and lactose have 1,4-glycosidic linkage.

(b) In sucrose, C1- of glucose is connected to C2- of fructose. In amylose, C1 of one glucose unit is attached to C4 of other glucose through -glycosidic linkage.

(c) Cellulose has 1,4--D-glycosidic linkage, but amylose has 1,4--D-glycosidic linkage.

(d) In lactose, C1- of galactose is linked to C4- of glucose.
